sections.h2: Who answers questions about a Madison County, KY tax bill?
sections.html:
Three Richmond offices split the work. The sheriff answers for the bill, the PVA answers for the value behind it, and the County Clerk answers for deeds and for overdue bills.

  • The Sheriff's Office sits at 135 W Irvine, Suite B01, in Richmond (859-623-1511). It posts a secure online portal for searching and paying bills, takes payments in person or by mail, and tells owners never to mail cash.
  • The Property Valuation Administrator handles assessed value and exemptions. The sheriff's tax page gives its number as 859-623-5410.
  • The Clerk's Richmond Branch, 321 N. Madison Ave., records deeds. A second branch at 304 Chestnut Street in Berea does vehicle and marriage license work.

Under KRS 134.119 the sheriff may also take payment from someone paying on the owner's behalf, handy when an heir or agent clears the bill ahead of a sale.

sections.h2: Why does Madison County differ from the rural counties around it?
sections.html:
Madison County is a college county that has been adding residents for decades. Eastern Kentucky University is in Richmond, Berea College is in Berea, and Berea and Richmond are the county's only cities. Census counts show the effect: 28,541 people in 1940, 53,352 in 1980, 82,916 in 2010 and 92,701 in 2020, with the July 2025 estimate at 101,696.

The county was set up in December 1785 and is named for James Madison. Daniel Boone and a party of settlers began Fort Boonesborough on the Kentucky River in 1775, and it is now a state historic site. Interstate 75, U.S. 25, U.S. 421 and KY 52 cross the county, which borders Fayette County to the north and Jessamine, Garrard, Rockcastle, Jackson, Estill and Clark counties around the rest of its edge.

Of 36,148 households at the 2020 census, 40.5 percent of occupied units were rented, and 8.1 percent of all units sat vacant. About 36 percent of residents lived in rural areas, so many sellers hold parcels in places such as Kingston, Waco or Speedwell rather than inside a city.

Working farmland is valued by what the ground earns rather than by what a developer might pay, a rule found in Section 172A of the state constitution. Ask the PVA to show how each of your acres is classified before you price a farm.

sections.h2: How big is the Madison County housing market?
sections.html:
Census Bureau estimates for 2020 to 2024 describe a county centered on its two campuses, with a median owner-occupied home value of $232,000.

The county gained 9.7 percent in population between the 2020 base and mid-2025. Employer establishments numbered 1,808 in 2023, with total payroll near $1.19 billion, and 2022 retail sales reached $1.76 billion.

The median age at the 2020 census was 35.6, and the county's decade-by-decade jumps tell the same story: up 27.6 percent in the 1970 count and 24.9 percent in 1980. Today 16.1 percent of residents are 65 or older, 20.4 percent are under 18, and 5,522 are veterans. Households average 2.43 people, 84.2 percent of residents were in the same house a year earlier, and per capita income is $32,828. Roughly 16.4 percent of residents live below the poverty line.

sections.h2: When does a Madison County tax bill start costing extra?
sections.html:
The sheriff's tax page does not publish a dated calendar and tells owners to follow the periods printed on the bill or in the online portal. The standard timetable behind those periods is in KRS 134.015.

  • A full payment made by the first of November takes two percent off.
  • The following two months, through December, call for the face amount.
  • During January a five percent charge appears.
  • From February onward the charge is ten percent of the unpaid tax.

When bills are delayed, the Department of Revenue can substitute a shorter schedule that starts from the mailing date. Collection fees are layered on top for delinquent bills, and the Department of Revenue's guide says interest of one percent a month runs once the bill reaches the clerk.

The Madison County Clerk's home page carries a 2025 delinquent county property tax list in two parts, marked as updated August 31, 2026, plus a page for third-party purchasers. Pull your own parcel up there before you list. The County Attorney's office also runs delinquent collection and says an installment agreement signed before the Clerk's sale keeps a bill from being bought by an investor. Its number is 624-4777, extension 9.

sections.h2: What is the route for disputing a Madison County valuation?
sections.html:
Begin with a conference at the PVA. If that fails, a written petition goes to the County Clerk and the county board hears the case, a process laid out in KRS 133.120 and last amended effective July 15, 2026. Bring comparable sales, an appraisal or insurance records, and keep paying on the figure you claim while the dispute runs.

Near either campus, the best comparables are recent sales of similar houses on nearby streets. For acreage, ask the PVA which agricultural class applies. KRS 133.030 schedules the board to convene 25 to 35 days after the inspection period closes.

sections.h2: Does Madison County offer a senior or disability homestead exemption?
sections.html: It does. The deduction for 2025 and 2026 is $49,100, which would lower a $232,000 home to a taxable $182,900. It is open to owner-occupants who are 65 or older or classified as totally disabled, and the Madison County PVA takes the application. A buyer who qualifies files separately after closing.

sections.h2: What should be settled before a Madison County closing?
sections.html:
Get a payoff figure from the sheriff for this year's bill and scan the clerk's delinquent list for earlier years. The sheriff's page notes that property taxes are commonly prorated between buyer and seller, with the current owner answerable for payment, so check how your settlement statement divides the bill.

A tax lien can ride with the land for as long as eleven years under KRS 134.015(5), which is why title agents ask for payoff at the table.

Deeds go to the Clerk's Richmond Branch at (859) 624-4703, extension 3. The office keeps papers from 1786 onward, searchable by a person's name only, and has scanned everything since 1986 for viewing in person or through the paid ECCLIX service. Electronic filings are handled each morning until roughly 10:00. Owners can also enroll in DocAlert, a free notification that fires whenever a document is recorded under their name or property details. The state's transfer tax, fifty cents for each $500 of value under KRS 142.050, comes to $232 at the Census median value.

faqs.q: Can Madison County property tax be paid online?
faqs.a: Yes, through the sheriff's secure portal, which also lets you search bills. The portal displays any processing fee before you confirm, and paying at the Richmond office or by mail still works.

faqs.q: How large is the 2026 exemption for Madison County seniors?
faqs.a: $49,100, the same as for 2025. Owners 65 or older, or totally disabled, apply through the PVA.

faqs.q: Which Madison County office records a deed?
faqs.a: The Clerk's Richmond Branch at 321 N. Madison Ave. Call (859) 624-4703, extension 3, for the recordings desk.

faqs.q: Is there help when a Madison County bill has gone delinquent?
faqs.a: The County Attorney's delinquent tax program, at 624-4777 extension 9, can arrange installment payments if you sign before the Clerk's sale.

faqs.q: Who pays the Madison County tax bill when a house changes owners mid-year?
faqs.a: The sheriff says the current owner must make sure it is paid and that bills are commonly prorated at closing. Confirm the split with your closing agent.
